# E88 FULL gates, written 2026-11-02 before any FULL job ran

Written by Claude after the pilots and after the owner's ruling of 2026-11-02 ("Its oke if the network isn't
definitive tried and failed is still useful information"), which overrides the Q1 stop and the pilots' block
on FULL. results/E88/pilot_gates.md is unchanged and stands. Every pilot gate that failed stays failed. Numbers
from the FULL networks are reported beside those records and do not replace them.
At the time of writing: no 40,000-step network exists, no network has been judged on real data by any check
below (P6 only timed the failed 5,000-step network on 500 recording-7 frames), and recording 32 has been opened
by no network. Nothing here may be changed after it is written. Later notes go in the plan's dated section.

## Rules for every job
Cores 14,15, 2 threads or 2 workers, for every E88 job including audits and rebuilds (task instruction: this
replaces 0-9,11-13). Every job and every held GPU lock is appended to the scratch busy.log. GPU work holds
gpu_lock. offline CPUs 10,26 and machine-check count 1 are checked before each job and by a watcher every 30 s.
Memory cap 16 GB per job under memguard. Keep 30 GB free. Stored classical results are reused and not rerun.
The 3.1 h CPU comparison is skipped; P4's measured 44x is printed, labelled as a pilot rate. E88's wall times may
be inflated by waiting or by sharing the machine with E90 and are reported as such. Not a tuning run: no setting
or seed below may be chosen or changed by its result. A failed gate never stops the run; only a safety stop or a
broken run does. One resume after a crash that is not a safety stop.

## Fixed settings
Network A: base 32, 40,000 steps, seed 88, version A priors, code as in tools/run_e88_net.py.
Network B: warm start from A's final weights, fresh Adam, 12,000 steps (30%), seed 89, same schedule shape.
Training runs with XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true, because that is the only setting under which P8'
passed, and so that a resumed run is identical and not only equivalent. It costs about 4x in steps/s. Inference
does not use it. Checkpoint every 1,000 steps. Detection threshold 0.5, as in the pilots.
B's simulator (plan section 7), all from recording 7 only, per-block calibration:
- PSF: radial stack of up to 20,000 isolated bright spots: chosen K = 1 rows, N >= 2,000, sd < 30 nm, at least 3 px
  from the edge margin of 12 px, no other blob within 12 px in the frame; seed 885; bins 0.25 px to 12 px; local
  background is the median of the 9-12 px annulus, so wings beyond 9 px are not measured and are zero.
- Defocus: per-spot width scale w, least squares of the stacked profile on 2,000 of those spots; B draws
  w ~ LogNormal(0, sd of log w) per emitter. The sd includes fit noise and is not corrected.
- Background: the 30 block-median maps of recording 7 in photons, random 64 x 64 crop, random flips of both axes,
  same map for the three frames.
- Persistence: stay-on probability uniform on 0.3-0.7 per crop, stationary on-share as in A; a molecule keeps its
  position and photon count across the three frames.
- Density log-uniform 0.02-0.8 per um^2 per frame, brightness as A.
Real frames: primary calibration is P3's written action, per block and per recording, for both networks, which is
also the classical primary. The block-mean line of p3_line is a labelled sensitivity run for both, against the
classical line tables. Each frame uses its own block's values. The first and last frames repeat at the movie's
ends. Recording 32 plays no part in PSF, background, hyperparameters or tuning.

## P5 scale-up (owner's ruling)
validate at 40,000 steps with P5's code, seed 880 and movies. Lines unchanged: recall >= 0.90, RMSE <= 1.3 x CRLB, no
NaN. Reported as "at 40,000 steps". P5 at 5,000 steps stays NO-GO on the record. Same for B at its final step.

## P6, P7 and P8' on the record
P6's grid ratio is recomputed on the mean p map over all real frames of each recording, line 1.25, with P6's
trim and mod-8 code. The 500-frame NO-GO stands. P7's lines (r_hat <= 1.01, 0 divergences) are reported for the 200.
The written no-go said fewer spots; the owner's ruling says run as the plan describes, so 200 spots run, same seed
(887), same model, tune and draws as P7, default start, 4 chains, 2 at a time. P8' stands as recorded.

## Section 7 checks on real frames
Recording 32 is the judged recording for both networks; recording 7 is reported beside it. All inside the mask.

**Check 1, paired frames.** gap 3, radius 1.5 px, b.link_pairs and fit_z_scale, good_rows filter, bootstrap over
tracks, 400 draws. Matched brightness: pair brightness sqrt(N1 N2), 8 bins at quantiles of the reference's pairs,
each pair weighted by reference share over own share; a bin the method lacks is dropped and the dropped share of
the reference is reported. Reference primary is classical chosen K, with K = 1 beside it. Unweighted z is reported too.
Absolute lines: pass 1.0-1.15, failure over 1.25, between them undefined. Relative line (Q8, from pilot_gates.md):
"no worse than classical" if z <= classical z, "worse" if z > 1.10 x classical z, otherwise "between".
Q7: 95% half-width and one se side by side. Gap 1 and radii 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3 px are shown beside it, not gating.
Simulated baseline: one movie, b.simulate_linked_movie, 2,000 frames, recording 7's block 0 median background,
20,000 events, stay-on 0.55, sites and brightness resampled from classical rows, seed 886, read by classical and
by A and B, whole field. It tests the method and says nothing about the microscope.

**Check 2, companion halo.** Same-frame pairs. Bright: N >= 2,000 inside the mask. Faint: N < 1,000, anywhere. Rows
past the edge filter but not past the sd filter, because a faint row is what this looks for. Density of faint
per bright per um^2 against distance, 50 nm bins to 1,500 nm. Ring 301-462 nm; far field 1,000-1,500 nm. Failure:
ring density over 2 x far field. Classical chosen K beside each network.

**Check 3, population replicate.** Population, not frames: windows of 100 frames at 1000, 7000, 13000. Each
window's emitter rate is the method's own count per frame there; sites and brightness resampled independently
from that method's rows at least 500 frames away from the window; background is the window's rolling median; PSF
Gaussian 1.05 px for A and empirical with defocus for B; exact EMCCD noise; no persistence. Seed 889. Blobs are
read with b.detect on real and replicate alike. Blob area, peak above background and normalised radial profile
are compared. No line was written, so none is invented: KS distances and the profile ratio at 3-7 px are reported.
Lineup: nine 40 x 40 panels, one real, position drawn by the seeded rng, stored for the notebook. Fitted emitters
are never rendered on to their own frames.

**Check 4, NUTS audit.** 200 spots, 100 chosen K = 1 and 100 chosen K = 2, from the recording-7 mask. Line: median
NUTS sd / Laplace sd within 0.8-1.25, over all 200, with K = 1, K = 2 and converged-only medians beside it. Position
agreement and sd ratio with each network, nearest row in the frame within 1.5 px. The converged-only medians are
descriptive, because r_hat decides which spots enter them.

**Coverage on simulation (certificate).** Cells: photons 500, 1000, 2000, 4000 by density 0.02, 0.089, 0.3, 0.7, 1.5
per um^2 (1.5 lies outside the training prior and is marked so), background 110 photons, 40 frames, seed 881.
Two worlds: "gauss" (A's world, P5's movie) and "empirical" (B's PSF, defocus, recording-7 background map of block 10,
stay-on 0.5). Per cell: recall and precision at 2 px, RMSE / CRLB, 95% coverage per axis, median |error / sd| scaled
by 1.4826, sum p / true count. Near-nominal: 95% coverage within 0.90-0.98. Not a go/no-go for anything.

## Decision (section 2)
The written rule, grid and bands exactly as P2b's: same drift method (leave-block-out per recording, on the
method's own rows), same 30 nm filter, same merging, same Field, 200 draws, same seeds. N* per recording and for
both. "The network changes the decision" means the network's N for both differs from the classical 10,500. Stored
classical results are the reference. The classical N stays 10,500 on the written rule, and 12,000 under the line.
Random-split against block-split FRC at 15,000 frames: localisations unmerged, random half, against events
merged, 50-frame blocks, all methods.

## Outcomes (section 7)
A failure "appears" for a network if on recording 32 its paired z is over 1.25, or "worse" on the relative line, or
its halo ratio is over 2. Outcome A: A fails and B passes every check A failed (z <= 1.25, not "worse", halo <= 2).
Outcome B: A fails and B does not. Outcome C: A does not fail. Outcome D is read independently: B's N, or A's if B
does not exist, equals the classical N. The headline follows from these, and if the network fails the headline says so,
keeps the classical frames answer as the result on real data, and claims nothing beyond what was measured.
Out of domain: four 532 frames at 3000-3003 of dSTORM532_Nc82_7.tif by range request, through A and B, red calibration.
The certificate says "never tested here" whatever the output looks like.
